messages:
Rachel Singh: FYI support got a customer escalation during our internal midnight load window — lots of 429s + tail latency spikes. They ran a replay of production traffic and saw sustained 500ms+ P95 and ~20% 429s. Filed a ticket, escalated to SRE.
Maya Chen: thanks rachel. any idea if they used a real API key or test key? important for quota routing.
Rachel Singh: they said they used org API key bound to hosted tier (not dedicated). Replay script attached in ticket.
Sam Patel: pinging this here — timeline? did this coincide with the k8s job that started the canary rollout?
Carlos Diaz: I saw a spike at 00:12 UTC, correlates with our daily internal loadcook test (scheduled burst ramp). Deploy bot also shows a canary deploy finishing ~00:10 but no errors.
incident-bot: Deploy "canary-edge-v2" succeeded in prod-us-west at 00:09:55 UTC :white_check_mark:
Luca Romano: ok two possible layers: 1) rate-limit/quota exhaustion on hosted tier, 2) KV cache & batching causing queueing -> tail latency. Need repro steps and headers.
Rachel Singh: customer provided sample response headers: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rw-rate-limit-limit: 1200
x-rw-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rw-rate-limit-reset: 167
x-rw-burst-available: 0
x-rw-quota-monthly: 500000
```
Maya Chen: interesting. limit 1200 (RPM?) and burst=0 available. If their replay hammered concurrent TPM, the per-minute might be OK but burst depleted. Do we still allow short bursts via token bucket?
Sam Patel: current hosted defaults config (prod) for new orgs: RPM=800, TPM=4000, burst_tokens=200. but many long-running replays can drain burst quickly.
Carlos Diaz: customer said they replayed at 200 RPS for 3 minutes then kept 50 RPS steady. That will consume bucket fast.
Luca Romano: to reproduce, we should run our internal replay runner but with a long tail: ramp 1 -> 200 RPS over 30s, hold 3m, drop to 50 RPS for 10m. Also capture headers, latency, and internal queue depth metrics (kv-cache hits, batching size).
Maya Chen: agreed. repro command (k6) we used before:
```
k6 run --vus 200 --duration 4m script.js --out json=out.json
# script.js replays requests with same path, auth header
```
Rachel Singh: customer also reported intermittent 502s when 429s started — could be our fallback to edge-tier instances hitting overloaded worker pools.
Sam Patel: action: SRE to run a controlled variant in staging that mirrors hosted capacity and rate-limit profile. We should try multiple hosted default sets to find sane defaults. Proposals:
- Conservative: RPM=600, TPM=3000, burst=100
- Balanced: RPM=1000, TPM=6000, burst=300
- Aggressive: RPM=1800, TPM=12000, burst=800
Please vote or propose numbers.
Carlos Diaz: prefer Balanced as starting point. Most apps need some burst for short warm-ups. Also add a grace policy for replay keys (bot/test keys) that throttles differently.
Maya Chen: +1 Balanced. But also want to run automated loadscript that does 10 repeats with different seed timings to capture worst-case token-bucket depletion.
Luca Romano: I'll instrument runtime to expose token-bucket state in debug trace (only in staging) and add a short admin endpoint to drain/reseed the bucket for repro. Example internal curl: 
```
curl -X POST https://staging-admin.internal/ratebucket/reset 
-H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_KEY" 
-d '{"org_id":"acct-1234","reset_to":300}'
```
Rachel Singh: for support playbook: 1) ask if they used org key vs dedicated; 2) ask for request density (RPS/RPM), replay script; 3) ask for response headers (x-rw-rate-limit-*); 4) advise a staged replay at lower RPS to avoid breaking prod.
Sam Patel: good. another troubleshooting tip: check the routing policy for that org — if fallback to cheaper model variant was enabled it might have different concurrency limits. Also check per-model concurrency caps.
Maya Chen: test plan for eng-sre:
1) Create a staging org with hosted-capacity profile (slots matching prod).
2) Run k6 ramp tests for the three proposals (Conservative/Balanced/Aggressive).
3) Capture metrics: 429%, P50/P95/P99, queuing latency, batching sizes, token-bucket level.
4) Evaluate cost delta for each profile via billing-sim script.
5) Recommend a default profile (and separate default for replay/test keys).

I'll own step 2-3 if Sam + Carlos can help with provisioning.

Carlos Diaz: I can provision staging cluster with 4 gpu workers and attach probe metrics.

Luca Romano: I will push the debug trace and admin reset endpoint to staging by EOD.

Sam Patel: I'll run the billing-sim and help analyze cost/latency tradeoffs.

Rachel Singh: support note for customer: we are reproducing in staging and will suggest either moving to Dedicated for predictable throughput or recommended replay pattern. I'll keep them updated.

Maya Chen: one more ask — add an automated regression test in CI that runs a fast ramp (30s to 200 RPS hold 30s) against a small cluster and fails if 429 rate > 5% or P95 > 350ms. This will catch accidental regressions to throttling behavior.

Sam Patel: +1. let's also add ephemeral dashboards for these runs so PMs can eyeball.

Rachel Singh: noted. I've updated the ticket with these action items and assigned to eng-sre. I'll ping again after the first staging run. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Summary created: "loadtest-repro-1823001234" — owners: Maya C, Sam P, Luca R; priority: P2
Maya Chen: thanks everyone. starting the first run in ~15m and will paste raw headers/metrics here. :eyes:
